hop3_docs: Kirsten Dunst | Kirsten Caroline Dunst ( ; born April 30, 1982) is an American actress.  She made her film debut in Woody Allen's short film "Oedipus Wrecks" for the anthology film "New York Stories" (1989).  At the age of twelve, Dunst gained widespread recognition as Claudia in "Interview with the Vampire" (1994), a role for which she was nominated for a Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actress.  She appeared in "Little Women" the same year and in "Jumanji" the following year.  After a recurring role in the third season of the NBC medical drama "ER" (1996–97) as Charlie Chemingo and starring in films such as "Wag the Dog" (1997), "Small Soldiers" (1998), the 1998 English dub of "Kiki's Delivery Service" (1989), and "The Virgin Suicides" (1999), Dunst began making romantic comedies and comedy-dramas, starring in "Drop Dead Gorgeous" (1999), "Bring It On" (2000), "Get Over It" and "Crazy/Beautiful" (both released in 2001).
